matters. An inventory count, or a health, licensing or tidiness check, usually lists nothing.

### A requirement another suite already checks (shims)

Benchmarks overlap: CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester tests often read the same setting. Before writing a check for a
benchmark requirement, and when reviewing one:

1. **Find the tests in every suite that read the setting.** `Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key> |
   Format-Table Id, Title`, and search `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name.
2. **Read the benchmark's own sources**, not only the requirement's one-line text: its audit or assessment
   guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (CIS audit and remediation sections; the SCuBA baseline
   and ScubaGear; for ASD the ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure
   Cloud). Note every concrete value: a number of days, a threshold, a role list, an authentication strength, a
   rule that must be Block. Use the web tools; cite the page.
3. **Decide:**
   - Same check: write a **shim**, a test with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control`, `Author` and `.md` whose body is
     `return <the other test's function>` (`return Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser`).
   - Same check, different value that the other test takes as a parameter: a shim with its own parameter whose
     default is the benchmark's value, passed on (`return Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold -MaximumLockoutThreshold $MaximumLockoutThreshold`).
   - Something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a check of its own. Read data through
     `internal/services/<service>/` helpers, and move a helper there (with a neutral name) when another suite
     already has the code; never copy another check's logic or name a generic helper after a suite.

A shim declares the same `Product`, `RelatedProduct`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`,
`UserImpact`, `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `License`, `Permission`, `TenantType`, `Cloud`,
`Platform`, `Lifecycle`, `LongRunning` and `Exclusive` as the test it calls; calls a test that is not a shim;
passes only parameters that test declares; leaves its own requirement off that test's `Control`; and says in its
`.md` what the benchmark asks and which test it runs, by ID. `powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1`
enforces all of this. The full guidance, with an example, is
[Tests that another suite already has](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).

When reviewing, fail a benchmark check that re-implements a check another suite already has when the benchmark's
sources give no reason for the difference, and say which test it duplicates and which source you read.

### What a benchmark check evaluates

A CIS check does what the benchmark's **PowerShell audit procedure** does: the same objects, the same pass
condition. When the UI steps and the PowerShell steps differ, follow the PowerShell steps.

- **Scope.** The audit reads every object → the check reads every object, including ones that apply to no user
  (CIS 6.2.1 checks `AutoForwardingMode` on every `Get-HostedOutboundSpamFilterPolicy` result). The audit reads
  one object → the check reads only that one (CIS 2.1.15 uses `-Identity Default`, so no custom policies). Never
  narrow a check to the policies users receive, or widen it beyond what the audit reads.
- **Values.** Use the thresholds the audit names or its script sets (CIS 2.1.11: 90% of the extension list). Make
  one a parameter, defaulting to the benchmark's value, when organizations may need another.
- **Missing data.** The object the audit reads is not returned → fail or error, never pass.

An effective-policy view belongs in an MT check. For CISA, read the SCuBA baseline and ScubaGear's policy in place
of the CIS audit. When reviewing, fail a benchmark check whose scope, values or missing-data handling differ from
the audit procedure without a reason from the benchmark, and quote the audit step. The full guidance is
[What a benchmark test evaluates](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx#what-a-benchmark-test-evaluates).

### Where the keys come from

- `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` take keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`: the
  products with their features, the areas and the resource types. A feature key belongs to one product.
- `Product` follows the folder: a check in `tests/maester/entra` or `tests/cisa/entra` is `entra`. The folder map
  is in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`; a new service folder needs an entry there.
- `Mitre` takes technique IDs from the pinned ATT&CK release, `powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`.
  An ID that the release retired or does not know fails the unit tests. Tactics are looked up from the ID and
  never typed.
- `Control` takes requirement IDs from the framework files (`tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`) and NIST
  control IDs from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`. The unit tests fail on an ID that is in neither.
- `Get-MtTest -Product entra -Feature conditional-access | Format-Table Id, Title, Severity, Area, ResourceType`
  lists the existing checks of a feature, to compare your values with.
- **A new key is added to the taxonomy in the same pull request as the first test that uses it.** Prefer an
  existing key. Do not add a key ahead of its test: the unit tests fail on a product, feature, area or resource
  type that no test uses. A new area also needs a row in the rubric's area table, which the unit tests compare
  with the taxonomy.

### Tags

`Tag` holds free labels for the owner of a test folder. It is not how Maester classifies a check.

- Built-in checks carry no tag for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence, severity or their own ID.
  Each of those has an attribute or is derived, and the unit tests fail a built-in check that tags one. Remove
  such a tag when you edit an older check.
- Do not put `Preview` or `LongRunning` in `Tag`; use `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag.
- Users select checks with `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`, `-Severity` and `-Suite` on `Invoke-Maester` and
  `Get-MtTest`. The tags of Maester 2.x, such as `CA` or `CIS`, still select the checks that carried them, with a
  warning, through `powershell/assets/Maester.LegacyTags.json`. That file is generated and never edited, and a
  check added after 3.0 is not in it, so do not add a tag to make a new check selectable.
- A user's custom test may tag freely.

### How the values are checked

The unit tests in `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check what is mechanical. The
`attribute-review` check on the pull request has a reviewer model judge each new or changed value against the
rubric. The person or agent who reviews the pull request applies the same rubric. See
[How the rubric is enforced](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md#how-the-rubric-is-enforced).

When the attribute review fails, change the value, or explain in the pull request why the declared value fits
the rubric. When you review a check yourself, follow "Reviewing a test's attributes" in
[AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md); it also shows how to run the attribute review before you push.

## Step-by-Step Workflow: Creating a New Check

1. **Look for a test that already checks it**, in every suite, and for a benchmark requirement read the
   benchmark's own sources. If the benchmark asks for what an existing test checks, the new check is a shim; see
   [A requirement another suite already checks](#a-requirement-another-suite-already-checks-shims).
2. **Reserve an ID.** Check [issue #697](https://github.com/maester365/maester/issues/697) and comment to reserve
   the next `MT.xxxx` (the maester-issue-manager agent can do this). `Get-MtTest MT.12*` shows which IDs exist.
3. **Scaffold** with `New-MtTest -Id <ID> -Title '...' -Service <service> -Product <product key>
   -Path ./tests/<suite>/<service>`.
4. **Fill in the attribute**: `License`, `Author`, flags as needed.
5. **Write the function**: read with `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or the helpers, decide, `Add-MtTestResultDetail`,
   return a boolean. Add parameters for tunable values.
6. **Write the guide, the `.md`**, in full: a one-line summary, why the setting matters, numbered remediation
   steps with a direct link to the admin portal page, related links (Microsoft Learn, and the benchmark when the
   check maps to one), and the results footer. Replace every placeholder that `New-MtTest` wrote; a check with
   scaffold text in its guide is not finished. Verify product facts and links with Microsoft Learn.
7. **Choose the attribute values** with the rubric: `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
   `ImplementationCost`, `Mitre`, `Control`, and `RelatedProduct` when one applies. See
   [Choosing the attribute values](#choosing-the-attribute-values) and
   [Framework requirements and NIST controls](#framework-requirements-and-nist-controls-control). The
   [test builder](https://maester.dev/test-builder) shows the allowed values and the rubric for each attribute
   and writes the attribute; use it to check a value you are unsure of.
8. **Validate offline**: `Import-Module ./powershell/Maester.psd1 -Force; Get-MtTest <ID>` must show
   `IsValid = True` and no `Errors`. Name the ID and leave out `-Path`: `Get-MtTest -Path <file>` applies the
   rules of a custom test, so it does not report a missing attribute or a key that is not in the taxonomy.
9. **Run against a tenant**: `Connect-Maester; Invoke-MtTest -Path <file>` (or `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`). Try
   `-Parameter @{...}` for each parameter. Check the row's `Result`, `ReasonCode`, `ResultDetail.TestResult`.
10. **Run the unit tests**: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`. `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestLint.Tests.ps1`
   and `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` check every built-in test.

## Converting a User's Pester-format Test

Users' 2.x custom tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) still run when Pester 5.7.1+ is installed. To convert:

```powershell
Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom -WhatIf
Convert-MtTest -Path ./custom | Format-Table Id, Status, Notes
```

It writes `Test.<ID>.ps1` + `.md` per `It`, turns a `Test-MtConnection` guard into `Service`, removes a blanket
`-SkippedBecause Error` catch, and rewrites a trailing `| Should -Be $true` to `return`. The `Describe` name
becomes `Feature`, so the row's `Block` stays what it was. The Pester tags are kept in `Tag`, except that a
`Preview` tag becomes `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and a `LongRunning` tag the `LongRunning` flag. Rows marked
`NeedsReview` have `TODO` comments; tests with names built at run time are `Skipped` and must be rewritten as
families. Once converted, delete the Pester file: the native test runs and the Pester test with the same ID no
longer does.

A user's custom native test lives in their `custom/` folder, uses their own ID prefix (not `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `MT1060.`, or `MP.`, which is reserved for Maester Packs), needs a `.md`, and needs only `Id` and `Title` in its attribute.
It may set `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` to values of its own (a value that matches the taxonomy
is stored as the key), may tag freely and may use `Control`; the rubric applies to it only if its owner wants it
to. It can call only Maester's exported commands; to reuse a built-in check it calls `Invoke-MtTest -Id <ID>`.

## Validation Checklist

### Test logic
- [ ] Returns exactly one `$true`/`$false`; no stray pipeline output.
- [ ] A benchmark check reads the same objects and uses the same pass condition as the benchmark's PowerShell
      audit procedure, and fails or errors when the audited object is not returned.
- [ ] No other suite already checks the same setting; or the benchmark's own sources were read and the check is
      a shim of that test, or differs from it for a reason those sources give.
- [ ] No `Test-MtConnection` guard, no `Get-MtLicenseInformation` check; `Service` and `License` declared instead.
- [ ] No blanket `try { } catch { Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error ... }`.
- [ ] `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` (not `$null`) when the check does not apply.
- [ ] Data retrieval uses `Invoke-MtGraphRequest` or Maester helpers.
- [ ] No hard-coded GUIDs, tenant IDs or names; tunables are described parameters.
- [ ] No writes to `$script:`, `$global:`, `$env:` or `$__MtSession`.
- [ ] `Platform = 'Windows'` if it uses Windows-only commands.

### Attribute and files
- [ ] `Test.<Id>.ps1` and `Test.<Id>.md` in the right suite folder; ID unique and not reused.
- [ ] `Id`, `Title`, `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `Mitre`, `Service`, `Author` set;
      values constant.
- [ ] `UserImpact` and `ImplementationCost` set, or both left out when `Severity` is `Info`.
- [ ] `Product`, `Feature`, `Area` and `ResourceType` are keys from `powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`; a
      new key is added there in this pull request.
- [ ] Each of those values, and `RelatedProduct` if set, checked against its section of the
      [attribute rubric](../../../website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md), with the reason visible in
      the description or the remediation text.
- [ ] No `Category` or `Preview`; no `Tag` for product, feature, area, suite, benchmark, licence,
      severity or the ID. `Lifecycle = 'Preview'` and the `LongRunning` flag where they apply.
- [ ] A CIS, CISA or ASD check sets `Control` to its requirement (`cis-m365:<id>`, `cis-github:<id>`, `essential-eight:<id>` or
      `cisa-scuba:<id>`), first, and the requirement is in the suite's framework file.
- [ ] `Control` was considered for every check: a CIS or CISA requirement that asks for the same setting, and
      NIST SP 800-53 controls from `powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json` (none when a `cisa-scuba`
      reference already brings them). Left empty only when nothing applies.
- [ ] `[CmdletBinding()]` and `[OutputType([bool])]`; comment-based help inside the function.
- [ ] `Get-MtTest <ID>` (without `-Path`) reports no errors.

### Documentation
- [ ] `.md` has summary, rationale, `#### Remediation action` with portal links, and ends with `<!--- Results --->` + `%TestResult%`.
- [ ] No scaffold placeholder is left in the `.md` ("Describe what this test checks", "Explain how to fix"), and its links open the page they name.
- [ ] Pass message starts with "Well done."; fail message is actionable.

﻿function Test-MtCisIdleSessionTimeout {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Checks that idle session timeout is 3 hours or less and that a Conditional Access policy applies it to unmanaged devices.

    .DESCRIPTION
        Checks that an activity-based timeout policy sets the web session idle timeout to no more than the allowed number of hours, and that an enabled Conditional Access policy uses app enforced restrictions for browser sessions of Microsoft 365 apps.
        CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 (1.3.2, L2)

    .EXAMPLE
        Test-MtCisIdleSessionTimeout

        Returns true if the idle session timeout is 3 hours or less and a Conditional Access policy enforces it for browsers.

    .LINK
        https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.1.3.2
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.1.3.2',
        Title = 'Ensure ''Idle session timeout'' is set to ''3 hours (or less)'' for unmanaged devices',
        Product = 'microsoft-365',
        RelatedProduct = 'entra',
        Feature = 'organization-settings',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = 'T1550.004',
        Control = ('cis-m365:1.3.2', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-12'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Maximum idle session timeout in hours.
        [ValidateRange(1, 24)]
        [int] $MaximumIdleTimeoutHours = 3
    )

    Write-Verbose 'Getting the activity-based timeout policy and Conditional Access policies...'
    $timeoutPolicies = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/activityBasedTimeoutPolicies' | Where-Object { $_ })
    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy

    $timeoutSpan = $null
    if ($timeoutPolicies.Count -gt 0) {
        $definition = @($timeoutPolicies[0].definition)[0] | ConvertFrom-Json
        $timeout = $definition.ActivityBasedTimeoutPolicy.ApplicationPolicies[0].WebSessionIdleTimeout
        if ($timeout) {
            $timeoutSpan = [timespan]::Parse($timeout)
        }
    }
    $timeoutOk = $null -ne $timeoutSpan -and $timeoutSpan -le [timespan]::FromHours($MaximumIdleTimeoutHours)

    $candidates = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.sessionControls.applicationEnforcedRestrictions.isEnabled })
    $report = foreach ($policy in $candidates) {
        $apps = @($policy.conditions.applications.includeApplications)
        $clients = @($policy.conditions.clientAppTypes)
        $problems = @(Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem -Policy $policy -Users AllUsers -Applications 'Office365' -TargetedCondition ClientAppTypes)
        $checks = [ordered]@{
            'Scope covers the required users and apps' = $problems.Count -eq 0
            'Office 365 apps only' = $apps.Count -eq 1 -and $apps -contains 'Office365'
            'Browser clients only' = $clients.Count -eq 1 -and $clients -contains 'browser'
            'App enforced restrictions' = $policy.sessionControls.applicationEnforcedRestrictions.isEnabled -eq $true
            'Enabled' = $policy.state -eq 'enabled'
        }
        $failedChecks = @($checks.GetEnumerator() | Where-Object { -not $_.Value } | ForEach-Object { $_.Key })
        $failedText = $failedChecks -join ', '
        if ($problems.Count -gt 0) { $failedText += " ($($problems -join '; '))" }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $policy.displayName; State = $policy.state; Failed = $failedText; Pass = $failedChecks.Count -eq 0 }
    }
    $policyOk = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Pass }).Count -ge 1
    $testResult = $timeoutOk -and $policyOk

    $passText = 'The idle session timeout is limited and a Conditional Access policy enforces it for browser sessions.'
    $failText = if (-not $timeoutOk -and -not $policyOk) { "There is no idle session timeout of $MaximumIdleTimeoutHours hours or less, and no Conditional Access policy that enforces app restrictions for browsers." } elseif (-not $timeoutOk) { "There is no idle session timeout of $MaximumIdleTimeoutHours hours or less." } else { 'No Conditional Access policy enforces app restrictions for browser sessions of Microsoft 365 apps.' }

    $timeoutText = if ($timeoutSpan) { "$($timeoutSpan.TotalHours) hours" } else { 'Not configured' }
    $resultMd = "| Setting | Value | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    $resultMd += "| Web session idle timeout | $timeoutText | $(if ($timeoutOk) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"
    $resultMd += "| Conditional Access policy with app enforced restrictions | $(if ($policyOk) { 'Found' } else { 'Not found' }) | $(if ($policyOk) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"
    foreach ($row in $report) {
        $resultMd += "| $($row.Name) ($($row.State)) | $(if ($row.Failed) { $row.Failed } else { 'None' }) | $(if ($row.Pass) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"
    }

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. $passText`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "$failText`n`n%TestResult%"
    }
    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

    <#
    .SYNOPSIS

    .DESCRIPTION

        Id = 'CISA.MS.AAD.4.1',
        Title = 'Security logs SHALL be sent to the agency''s security operations center for monitoring.',

        Severity = 'High',

    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]

    )

    $logs = Invoke-AzRestMethod -Method GET -Path "/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettingsCategories?api-version=2017-04-01-preview"
    $logs = ($logs.Content|ConvertFrom-Json).value
    $logs = ($logs | Where-Object { `
        $_.properties.categoryType -eq "Logs"
    }).name

    $configs = @()

    $settings = Invoke-AzRestMethod -Method GET -Path "/providers/microsoft.aadiam/diagnosticSettings?api-version=2017-04-01-preview"

    $settings = ($settings.Content|ConvertFrom-Json).value

    $settings | ForEach-Object { `

    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace "%TestResult%", $result

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown

    return $testResult

        # Check Global Administrator role only
        [switch]$GlobalAdminOnly
    )

    $EntraIDPlan = Get-MtLicenseInformation -Product EntraID
    $hasLicense = $EntraIDPlan -eq "P2" -or $EntraIDPlan -eq "Governance"
    if (-not $hasLicense) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotLicensedEntraIDP2OrGovernance
        return $null
    }

    $roles = Get-MtRole -CisaHighlyPrivilegedRoles
    if ($GlobalAdminOnly) {

                $_.id -eq "62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10"
        }
    } else {
        $roles = $roles | Where-Object {`
                $_.id -ne "62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10"
        }
    }

    $rolePolicies = @()

    foreach ($role in $roles) {
        $rolePolicy = [PSCustomObject]@{
            role             = $role.displayName
            activationNotify = $false
        }
        $policySplat = @{
            ApiVersion      = "v1.0"
            RelativeUri     = "policies/roleManagementPolicyAssignments"
            Filter          = "scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole' and roleDefinitionId eq '$($role.id)'"
            QueryParameters = @{
                expand = "policy(expand=rules)"
            }
        }
        $policy = Invoke-MtGraphRequest @policySplat

        $activationNotify = $policy.policy.rules | Where-Object {`
                $_.id -eq "Notification_Admin_EndUser_Assignment" -and `
                $_.notificationRecipients
        }
        $rolePolicy.activationNotify = -not $null -eq $activationNotify

        $rolePolicies += $rolePolicy
    }

    $misconfigured = $rolePolicies | Where-Object {`
            -not $_.activationNotify
    }

    $testResult = ($misconfigured | Measure-Object).Count -eq 0

    $link = "https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/ResourceMenuBlade/~/roles/resourceId//resourceType/tenant/provider/aadroles"
    $resultFail = "❌ Fail"
    $resultPass = "✅ Pass"

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant has notifications for [role activations]($link).`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant does not have notifications on [role activations]($link).`n`n%TestResult%"
    }

    $result = "| Role Name | Result |`n"
    $result += "| --- | --- |`n"

    foreach ($item in $rolePolicies) {
        $itemResult = $resultFail
        if ($item.activationNotify) {
            $itemResult = $resultPass
        }
        $result += "| $($item.role) | $($itemResult) |`n"
    }
    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace "%TestResult%", $result

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown

    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtCisPasswordExpiry {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks if passwords are set to expire

    .DESCRIPTION
    Passwords should not be set to expire
    CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 (1.3.1, L1)

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtCisPasswordExpiry

    Returns true if no passwords are set to expire

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtCisPasswordExpiry
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.1.3.1',
        Title = 'Ensure the ''Password expiration policy'' is set to ''Set passwords to never expire (recommended)''',
        Product = 'microsoft-365',
        RelatedProduct = 'entra',
        Feature = 'organization-settings',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Domain',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'None',
        Control = ('cis-m365:1.3.1', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-5(1)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        Author = 'NZLostboy',
        Contributor = ('merill', 'brianreidc7', 'blindzero')
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    Write-Verbose 'Get domain details for the password expiry period'
    $domains = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'domains'

    Write-Verbose 'Get verified and managed domains where passwords are set to expire'

    $noPasswordExpiryPeriodInDays = [int]::MaxValue

    $excludedDomains = @()
    $applicableDomains = @()
    foreach ($domain in $domains) {
        # Password policy checks apply only to managed and verified domains.
        if (($domain.authenticationType -ne "Managed") -or ($domain.isVerified -ne $true)) {
            $excludedDomains += $domain
            continue
        }

        $applicableDomains += $domain
    }

    $result = $applicableDomains | Where-Object {
        $passwordValidityPeriodInDays = 0
        $domainPasswordValidityPeriodInDays = $_.PasswordValidityPeriodInDays
        # If null or a boolean, the password expiry period is not set, and passwords do not expire.
        # Return false to indicate this domain does not fail the test.
        if (($null -eq $domainPasswordValidityPeriodInDays) -or ($domainPasswordValidityPeriodInDays -is [bool])) {
            return $false
        }
        if (-not [int]::TryParse($domainPasswordValidityPeriodInDays.ToString(), [ref]$passwordValidityPeriodInDays)) {
            return $false
        }
        # If valid integer, check if equal to the value that indicates no password expiry (MaxValue).
        return $passwordValidityPeriodInDays -ne $noPasswordExpiryPeriodInDays
    }

    $testResult = ($result | Measure-Object).Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant passwords are not set to expire on all your 'managed' and 'verified' domains:`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant has 1 or more 'managed' and 'verified' domains which expire passwords:`n`n%TestResult%"
    }

    $resultMd = "| Domain | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($item in $domains) {
        $itemResult = '❌ Fail'
        if ($item.id -in $excludedDomains.id) {
            $itemResult = '⏭️ Skip'
        } elseif ($item.id -notin $result.id) {
            $itemResult = '✅ Pass'
        }
        $resultMd += "| $($item.Id) | $($itemResult) |`n"
    }

    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Checks that the smart lockout threshold is not greater than the allowed maximum.

    .DESCRIPTION
        Checks that the smart lockout threshold in Microsoft Entra password protection does not exceed the maximum, which limits how many wrong passwords an attacker can try before the account is locked out. When the threshold is not stored, Microsoft Entra uses its public cloud default of 10.
        CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 (5.2.3.8, L1)

    .EXAMPLE
        Test-MtCisSmartLockoutThreshold

        Returns true if the lockout threshold is at most 10.

    .LINK
        https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.3.8
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.5.2.3.8',
        Title = 'Ensure that Account ''Lockout threshold'' is ''10'' or less',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'password-protection',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1110.001', 'T1110.003'),
        Control = ('cis-m365:5.2.3.8', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-7'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Maximum number of failed sign-ins before the account is locked out.
        [ValidateRange(1, 50)]
        [int] $MaximumLockoutThreshold = 10
    )

    Write-Verbose 'Getting the password rule settings...'
    $groupSettings = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'groupSettings'
    $passwordRules = @($groupSettings) | Where-Object { $_.templateId -eq '5cf42378-d67d-4f36-ba46-e8b86229381d' }
    $ruleValues = @{}
    foreach ($rule in $passwordRules.values) {
        $ruleValues[$rule.name] = $rule.value
    }

    # Microsoft's default lockout threshold applies when the setting is not stored.
    $default = 10
    $threshold = "$($ruleValues['LockoutThreshold'])"
    $isStored = $threshold -match '^\d+$'
    $effective = if ($isStored) { [int]$threshold } else { $default }
    $display = if ($isStored) { $threshold } else { "$default (default)" }
    $testResult = $effective -le $MaximumLockoutThreshold

    $passText = "The lockout threshold is $effective."
    $failText = "The lockout threshold is $effective. It should be $MaximumLockoutThreshold or less."

    $resultMd = "| Setting | Value | Maximum | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
    $resultMd += "| Lockout threshold | $display | $MaximumLockoutThreshold | $(if ($testResult) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. $passText`n`n%TestResult%"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "$failText`n`n%TestResult%"
    }
    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

﻿function Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that no enabled account with a privileged directory role has been inactive for 45 days or more.

    .DESCRIPTION
    ISM-1648 (Essential Eight, Restrict administrative privileges, Maturity Level Two) asks that privileged
    access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.

    The check lists the users with an active or eligible assignment to a directory role that Microsoft Entra
    marks as privileged, directly or through a role-assignable group, and reads the last sign-in of each. A
    user fails when the account is enabled and the most recent interactive or non-interactive sign-in is
    older than the number of days given (45 by default), or when the account has never signed in and was
    created before that. The emergency access accounts named in the Maester configuration
    (EmergencyAccessAccounts) are left out, because they are meant to stay unused.

    MT.1029 reports the same accounts through the Privileged Identity Management stale accounts alert, whose
    number of days each tenant sets. ASD names 45 days, so this check reads the sign-ins itself.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtAsdInactivePrivilegedAccess

    Returns true when every enabled privileged user signed in within the last 45 days.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1648
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'ASD.ISM-1648',
        Title = 'Privileged access to systems and their resources is disabled after 45 days of inactivity.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'roles',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('essential-eight:ISM-1648', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(3)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'jusso-dev'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Days without a sign-in after which privileged access must be disabled.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $InactiveDays = 45
    )

    $rolesOf = Get-MtPrivilegedRoleUser -ExcludeEmergencyAccessAccount
    if ($rolesOf.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }

    $cutoff = [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -UniqueId @($rolesOf.Keys) -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, accountEnabled, createdDateTime, signInActivity)
    $inactive = foreach ($user in $users) {
        if ($user.accountEnabled -ne $true) { continue }
        $signIns = @($user.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime, $user.signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { [datetime]$_ })
        $lastSignIn = if ($signIns.Count -gt 0) { ($signIns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum.ToUniversalTime() } else { $null }
        $isInactive = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff } else { $user.createdDateTime -and ([datetime]$user.createdDateTime).ToUniversalTime() -lt $cutoff }
        if ($isInactive) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                id                = $user.id
                displayName       = $user.displayName
                userPrincipalName = $user.userPrincipalName
                LastSignIn        = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { 'Never' }
                Roles             = $rolesOf[$user.id] -join ', '
            }
        }
    }
    $inactive = @($inactive)
    $testResult = $inactive.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Every enabled user with a privileged directory role signed in within the last $InactiveDays days ($($rolesOf.Count) users checked)."
    } else {
        $table = "| User | Last sign-in | Privileged roles |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in ($inactive | Sort-Object userPrincipalName)) { $table += "| $($user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.LastSignIn) | $($user.Roles) |`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($inactive.Count) enabled user(s) with a privileged directory role have not signed in for $InactiveDays days or more. Disable the account or remove the role, and let an access review or a PIM alert catch the next one.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

# operationApprovalPolicy resource type - Microsoft Graph beta | Microsoft Learn

Namespace: microsoft.graph

> 
> **Important:** Microsoft supports Intune /beta APIs, but they are subject to more frequent change. Microsoft recommends using version v1.0 when possible. Check an API's availability in version v1.0 using the Version selector.

> 
> **Note:** The Microsoft Graph API for Intune requires an [active Intune license](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=839381) for the tenant.

The OperationApprovalPolicy entity allows an administrator to configure which operations require admin approval and the set of admins who can perform that approval. Creating a policy enables the multiple admin approval service to catch requests which are targeted by the specific policy type defined.

## Methods

| Method | Return Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [List operationApprovalPolicies](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-list) | [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) collection | List properties and relationships of the [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) objects. |
| [Get operationApprovalPolicy](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-get) | [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) | Read properties and relationships of the [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) object. |
| [Create operationApprovalPolicy](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-create) | [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) | Create a new [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) object. |
| [Delete operationApprovalPolicy](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-delete) | None | Deletes a [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy). |
| [Update operationApprovalPolicy](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-update) | [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) | Update the properties of a [operationApprovalPolicy](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy) object. |
| [retrieveApprovableOperations function](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-retrieveapprovableoperations) | [operationApprovalPolicySet](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicyset) collection |  |
| [retrieveOperationsRequiringApproval function](../intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicy-retrieveoperationsrequiringapproval) | [operationApprovalPolicySet](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicyset) collection |  |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | String | The unique identifier of the policy. This ID is assigned at when the policy is created. Read-only. This property is read-only. |
| displayName | String | Indicates the display name of the policy. Maximum length of the display name is 128 characters. This property is required when the policy is created, and is defined by the IT Admins to identify the policy. |
| description | String | Indicates the description of the policy. Maximum length of the description is 1024 characters. This property is not required, but can be used by the IT Admin to describe the policy. |
| lastModifiedDateTime | DateTimeOffset | Indicates the last DateTime that the policy was modified. The value cannot be modified and is automatically populated whenever values in the request are updated. For example, when the 'policyType' property changes from `apps` to `scripts`. The Timestamp type represents date and time information using ISO 8601 format and is always in UTC time. For example, midnight UTC on Jan 1, 2014 would look like this: '2014-01-01T00:00:00Z'. Returned by default. Read-only. This property is read-only. |
| policyType | [operationApprovalPolicyType](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicytype) | The policy type for the OperationApprovalPolicy. Possible values are: `unknown`, `app`, `script`, `operationApprovalPolicy`. Possible values are: `unknown`, `deviceAction`, `deviceWipe`, `deviceRetire`, `deviceRetireNonCompliant`, `deviceDelete`, `deviceLock`, `deviceErase`, `deviceDisableActivationLock`, `windowsEnrollment`, `compliancePolicy`, `configurationPolicy`, `appProtectionPolicy`, `policySet`, `filter`, `endpointSecurityPolicy`, `app`, `script`, `role`, `deviceResetPasscode`, `unknownFutureValue`, `operationApprovalPolicy`, `autopilot`, `windows365`, `deviceEnrollment`, `deviceUpdate`, `enrollmentRestriction`, `tenantConfiguration`, `tunnel`, `endpointPrivilegeManagement`, `deviceSecurityAction`. |
| policyPlatform | [operationApprovalPolicyPlatform](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicyplatform) | Indicates the applicable platform for the policy. Possible values are: `notApplicable`, `androidDeviceAdministrator`, `androidEnterprise`, `iOSiPadOS`, `macOS`, `windows10AndLater`, `windows81AndLater`, `windows10X`. Default value is `notApplicable`. Possible values are: `notApplicable`, `androidDeviceAdministrator`, `androidEnterprise`, `iOSiPadOS`, `macOS`, `windows10AndLater`, `windows81AndLater`, `windows10X`, `unknownFutureValue`. |
| policySet | [operationApprovalPolicySet](intune-rbac-operationapprovalpolicyset) | Indicates areas of the Intune UX that could support MAA UX for the current logged in IT Admin. This property is required, and is defined by the IT Admins in order to correctly show the expected experience. |

# ASD Essential Eight and ISM

Checks that verify a Microsoft 365 tenant against the
[Essential Eight maturity model](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model)
and the [Information security manual](https://www.cyber.gov.au/ism) (ISM), both published by the Australian Signals
Directorate (ASD). They are also known as the ACSC Essential Eight and the ACSC ISM; the Australian Cyber Security
Centre (ACSC) is part of ASD. ASD maps each requirement of the maturity model to an ISM control.

## Layout

- `suite.json` declares the suite (`ASD`) and its two frameworks, `essential-eight` and `ism`.
- `frameworks/essential-eight.json` and `frameworks/ism.json` are the catalogues of the two frameworks. They are
  generated from the ISM OSCAL release by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`; do not edit them by hand.
- `<service>/Test.ASD.<ISM control>.ps1` and `.md` are the checks, one folder per product (`entra/`, `intune/`).

## IDs and mapping

ASD publishes the maturity model with a
[mapping of every requirement to one ISM control](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight/essential-eight-maturity-model-ism-mapping)
(October 2024 edition), and the ISM OSCAL release ships that mapping as Essential Eight baseline profiles, so a
check is named after the control it implements: `ASD.ISM-1504` implements ISM-1504. Its attribute names the
requirement in the Essential Eight framework first, `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`, and the framework file
relates that requirement to `ism:ISM-1504`, which Maester adds to the result. A check for a control that the
maturity model does not use names the ISM directly, `Control = 'ism:ISM-0421'`.

The `Benchmark` of a result carries the facts of the requirement: the maturity level that first requires it
(`Level`: `ML1`, `ML2` or `ML3`) and the mitigation strategy or strategies (`Strategy`) from the Essential Eight framework, or the
guideline, section and classification applicability from the ISM.

A passing check is evidence for the control it names. It is not an assessment: an Essential Eight assessment also
covers endpoints, servers and processes that a tenant check cannot see.

## Checks that another suite already has

Where ASD asks for what a CIS, CISA or Maester test already checks, the ASD check is a shim: it declares its own
ID, title and `Control` and returns the result of that test (`ASD.ISM-1504` returns `Test-MtCisMfaForEveryUser`).
Where ASD names a different value, the shim passes it as a parameter (`ASD.ISM-1403` runs the CIS lockout check
with a maximum of 5). A check has logic of its own only where ASD's own sources (the ISM, the Essential Eight
assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud) ask for something no other test checks. See
[Tests that another suite already has](https://maester.dev/docs/next/writing-tests#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).

﻿function Get-MtTrustedNamedLocationId {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Returns the IDs of the named locations that are marked as trusted.

    .DESCRIPTION
        Conditional Access policies reference named locations by ID, so a policy that excludes
        a location tells you nothing about whether that location is trusted. This resolves the
        tenant's named locations and returns only the trusted ones, letting a check distinguish
        a genuine trusted-location exclusion from any other exclusion.

        Only IP named locations carry the isTrusted flag. Country named locations have no trust
        concept and are never returned.

        Returns an empty array when the tenant has no trusted named location.

    .EXAMPLE
        Get-MtTrustedNamedLocationId

        Returns the IDs of the trusted named locations in the tenant.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([string[]])]
    param ()

    $namedLocations = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'identity/conditionalAccess/namedLocations' -ApiVersion beta

    return [string[]]@($namedLocations |
            Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -match 'ipNamedLocation' -and $_.isTrusted -eq $true } |
            Select-Object -ExpandProperty id)
}

function Get-MtActivityBasedTimeout {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Returns the web session idle timeout that the tenant's activity-based timeout policy sets.

    .DESCRIPTION
        The idle session timeout in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy >
        Idle session timeout) is stored as an activity-based timeout policy in Microsoft Entra ID. Its definition is a
        JSON string whose WebSessionIdleTimeout value is a time span, such as 03:00:00.

        Returns an object with Timeout (a [timespan], or $null when no policy sets a timeout) and PolicyName (the
        display name of the policy that was read, or $null when there is none).

    .EXAMPLE
        (Get-MtActivityBasedTimeout).Timeout

        Returns the idle timeout as a time span, or $null when none is set.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param ()

    $policies = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/activityBasedTimeoutPolicies' | Where-Object { $_ })

    $timeout = $null
    $policyName = $null
    if ($policies.Count -gt 0) {
        $policyName = $policies[0].displayName
        $definition = @($policies[0].definition)[0] | ConvertFrom-Json
        $value = $definition.ActivityBasedTimeoutPolicy.ApplicationPolicies[0].WebSessionIdleTimeout
        if ($value) {
            $timeout = [timespan]::Parse($value)
        }
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Timeout    = $timeout
        PolicyName = $policyName
    }
}

function Get-MtUserLastSignIn {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Returns the time of a user's most recent sign-in, in UTC, from the signInActivity of a user object.

    .DESCRIPTION
        Reads the signInActivity that a users request returns when it selects that property. By default the latest of
        the interactive and the non-interactive sign-in is returned. With -InteractiveOnly only lastSignInDateTime is
        read, as some audit procedures do.

        Returns $null when the user has no recorded sign-in of the kind asked for.

    .EXAMPLE
        Get-MtUserLastSignIn -User $user

        Returns the latest interactive or non-interactive sign-in of $user, or $null.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([datetime])]
    param (
        # A user object from Microsoft Graph that includes signInActivity.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $User,

        # Read only the interactive sign-in (lastSignInDateTime).
        [switch] $InteractiveOnly
    )

    $values = if ($InteractiveOnly) {
        @($User.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime)
    } else {
        @($User.signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime, $User.signInActivity.lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime)
    }
    $signIns = @($values | Where-Object { $_ } | ForEach-Object { ([datetime]$_).ToUniversalTime() })
    if ($signIns.Count -eq 0) { return $null }
    return ($signIns | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum
}

function Get-MtDomainPasswordValidity {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Returns the password expiration period of each domain of the tenant.

    .DESCRIPTION
        The password expiration policy is stored per domain, as passwordValidityPeriodInDays. It applies only to
        domains that are verified and managed (not federated), so each domain is returned with IsApplicable.

        ValidityDays is the number of days a password is valid. NeverExpires is true when the value is the one
        Microsoft Entra ID uses for "never expire" (2147483647). IsSet is false when the domain stores no value; what
        applies then is not stated by the API, so each check decides how to report it.

    .EXAMPLE
        Get-MtDomainPasswordValidity | Where-Object IsApplicable

        Returns the verified, managed domains with their password expiration period.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param ()

    $neverExpires = [int]::MaxValue
    foreach ($domain in @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'domains')) {
        $raw = $domain.passwordValidityPeriodInDays
        $days = 0
        # A boolean or a value that is not a number means no period is stored.
        $isSet = ($null -ne $raw) -and ($raw -isnot [bool]) -and [int]::TryParse($raw.ToString(), [ref]$days)
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id           = $domain.id
            IsApplicable = ($domain.authenticationType -eq 'Managed') -and ($domain.isVerified -eq $true)
            IsSet        = $isSet
            ValidityDays = if ($isSet) { $days } else { $null }
            NeverExpires = $isSet -and $days -eq $neverExpires
        }
    }
}

function Get-MtRoleActivationNotificationRecipient {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
        Returns the additional recipients of the role activation alert of a directory role.

    .DESCRIPTION
        Privileged Identity Management sends a "Role activation alert" to the administrators when an eligible member
        activates a role. Its additional recipients are stored in the role's management policy, in the rule
        Notification_Admin_EndUser_Assignment (notificationRecipients). Returns those addresses, or nothing when the
        role sends the alert to no additional recipient.

    .EXAMPLE
        Get-MtRoleActivationNotificationRecipient -RoleDefinitionId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10'

        Returns the additional recipients of the activation alert of the Global Administrator role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([string[]])]
    param (
        # The ID of the directory role definition.
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [string] $RoleDefinitionId
    )

    $policySplat = @{
        ApiVersion      = 'v1.0'
        RelativeUri     = 'policies/roleManagementPolicyAssignments'
        Filter          = "scopeId eq '/' and scopeType eq 'DirectoryRole' and roleDefinitionId eq '$RoleDefinitionId'"
        QueryParameters = @{ expand = 'policy(expand=rules)' }
    }
    $assignment = Invoke-MtGraphRequest @policySplat
    $rule = @($assignment.policy.rules) | Where-Object { $_.id -eq 'Notification_Admin_EndUser_Assignment' } | Select-Object -First 1
    return [string[]]@($rule.notificationRecipients | Where-Object { $_ })
}

﻿function Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Returns Entra directory role assignments, active and PIM-eligible.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Reads directory role assignments the same way for every caller, so the decision of when the PIM
    APIs can be used is made in one place.

    With Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Governance, active assignments come from
    roleAssignmentScheduleInstances, filtered to assignmentType 'Assigned' so an eligible role that is
    temporarily activated is not also returned as active, and eligible assignments come from
    roleEligibilityScheduleInstances. Without those licenses, or when the PIM APIs reject the tenant
    license even though subscribedSkus reports a P2 service plan, active assignments come from
    roleAssignments and eligible assignments are not read.

    Each assignment gets an AssignmentType property of Active or Eligible. The result has two
    properties: Assignments, and EligibleChecked, which is true when eligible assignments were read.

    .EXAMPLE
    $roleAssignments = Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment
    $roleAssignments.Assignments | Where-Object AssignmentType -eq 'Eligible'

    Returns the PIM-eligible assignments of every directory role.

    .EXAMPLE
    (Get-MtDirectoryRoleAssignment -RoleId '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10' -ExpandPrincipal).Assignments.principal

    Returns the principals that are assigned, or eligible for, the Global Administrator role.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # Only return assignments of these role definitions. Assignments of every role are returned when omitted.
        # Up to three roles are read with one filtered request each; more are read in one request and filtered here.
        [guid[]]$RoleId,

        # The type of assignments to return. Default is both Eligible and Active.
        [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active', 'EligibleAndActive')]
        [string]$MemberStatus = 'EligibleAndActive',

        # Expand the assigned principal on each assignment.
        [switch]$ExpandPrincipal,

        # Only return these properties of each assignment.
        [string[]]$Select,

        # Skip the Graph cache and read the assignments from Graph.
        [switch]$DisableCache
    )

    function Get-Assignment {
        param(
            [string]$Uri,
            [string[]]$Filter,
            [ValidateSet('Eligible', 'Active')]
            [string]$AssignmentType,
            [bool]$Expand,
            [string[]]$Property,
            [bool]$NoCache
        )

        $params = @{
            ApiVersion   = 'v1.0'
            RelativeUri  = $Uri
            DisableCache = $NoCache
        }
        if ($Property) { $params.Select = $Property }
        $Filter = @($Filter | Where-Object { $_ })
        if ($Filter) { $params.Filter = $Filter -join ' and ' }
        if ($Expand) { $params.QueryParameters = @{ expand = 'principal' } }

        foreach ($assignment in @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest @params)) {
            if ($null -eq $assignment) { continue }
            # Copy before setting AssignmentType: property names are case-insensitive, so this replaces Graph's own
            # assignmentType, and the session cache returns these same objects to every later caller.
            $assignment | Select-Object -Property * |
                Add-Member -MemberType NoteProperty -Name 'AssignmentType' -Value $AssignmentType -Force -PassThru
        }
    }

function Test-MtOperationApprovalPolicies {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Check for the usage of Intune Multi Admin Approval Policies

    .DESCRIPTION
    At least one Intune Multi Admin Approval Policy should be configured.

    With RequiredPolicyType the check passes only when a policy of one of those types exists, for example
    deviceWipe or deviceAction for a policy that protects device wipes.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtOperationApprovalPolicies

    Returns true if at least one Intune Multi Admin Approval Policy is configured, false if none is configured.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtOperationApprovalPolicies -RequiredPolicyType deviceWipe, deviceAction

    Returns true if a Multi Admin Approval policy protects device wipes.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtOperationApprovalPolicies
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'MT.1096',
        Title = 'Ensure at least one Intune Multi Admin Approval policy is configured',
        Product = 'intune',
        Feature = 'tenant-administration',
        Area = 'privileged-access',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1072', 'T1078.004'),
        Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:AC-3(2)', 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-5(4)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'INTUNE_A',
        Author = 'nicolonsky'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'This test refers to multiple settings.')]
    param(
        # Policy types (operationApprovalPolicyType, such as deviceWipe) of which one policy must exist. Empty accepts any policy.
        [string[]] $RequiredPolicyType
    )

    Write-Verbose 'Testing Multi Admin Approval Policy configuration'
    Write-Verbose 'Retrieving Intune Multi Admin Approval Policies status...'
    $approvalPolicies = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'deviceManagement/operationApprovalPolicies' -ApiVersion beta | Where-Object { $_ })

    if ($RequiredPolicyType) {
        $matching = @($approvalPolicies | Where-Object { $_.policyType -in $RequiredPolicyType -or $_.policySet.policyType -in $RequiredPolicyType })
        $testResult = $matching.Count -gt 0
        $typeList = ($RequiredPolicyType | ForEach-Object { "``$_``" }) -join ', '
        $testResultMarkdown = if ($testResult) {
            "Well done. An Intune Multi Admin Approval policy of type $typeList is configured.`n"
        } else {
            "No Intune Multi Admin Approval policy of type $typeList is configured.`n"
        }
    } else {
        $testResult = $approvalPolicies.Count -gt 0
        $testResultMarkdown = if ($testResult) {
            "Well done. At least one Intune Multi Admin Approval Policy is configured.`n"
        } else {
            'No Intune Multi Admin Approval Policy is configured.'
        }
    }

    if ($approvalPolicies.Count -gt 0) {
        $testResultMarkdown += "| Name | Type |`n"
        $testResultMarkdown += "| --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($policy in $approvalPolicies) {
            $testResultMarkdown += "| $(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $policy.displayName) | $($policy.policyType) |`n"
        }
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

result.output:
## Feature

The part of the product the test is about. One key from the product's `Features` list.

- Choose the feature whose settings page or object type the remediation sends the admin to.
- When a test spans two features, choose the one that fails most directly. A Conditional Access policy that
  requires a compliant device is `conditional-access`, not `devices`.
- Tests that check the same thing get the same feature, whatever folder or suite they are in.
- A feature that would hold one test only is usually too narrow. Prefer an existing feature.

## Area

The security theme, whatever the product. One key.

| Key | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `authentication` | How an identity proves who it is: MFA, authentication methods, passwords, legacy protocols, Kerberos and NTLM hardening, session and token lifetime. |
| `privileged-access` | Administrative roles and accounts: who holds them, just-in-time elevation, emergency access, admin tiering, delegated admin rights. |
| `access-control` | Who may reach which resource under which conditions: device, location and risk conditions, permissions on objects, user defaults. |
| `applications` | App registrations, service principals and their credentials, consent and API permissions, OAuth apps, add-ins, connectors. |
| `external-access` | Guests, cross-tenant access, federation and trusts, external sharing and external communication. |
| `devices` | Device compliance, enrollment and configuration, endpoint protection, device identity. |
| `email-protection` | Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, mail flow rules, meeting and messaging protections. |
| `data-protection` | Data loss prevention, sensitivity labels, encryption, retention, backup. |
| `logging-and-detection` | Audit logs, diagnostic settings, alert policies, sensors and the health of detection tooling. |
| `identity-lifecycle` | Stale and dormant accounts, ownership, access reviews, entitlement management, group membership hygiene. |
| `infrastructure` | The directory and platform itself: domain controllers, DNS, replication, sites, schema, Group Policy health, protocol hardening, subscriptions, tenant-wide platform settings. |
| `engineering-systems` | DevOps organizations, repositories, pipelines, build identities, the software supply chain. |
| `ai` | AI agents and copilots: who can use and share them, how they authenticate, what data and tools they reach. |

When more than one area fits, choose by what the control is for, in this order:

1. It protects administrators or admin rights: `privileged-access`.
2. It decides how sign-in is proven: `authentication`.
3. It is about an application, service principal or agent as the subject: `applications`, or `ai` for agents.
4. It is about people or data outside the organization: `external-access`.
5. Otherwise the area that names the mechanism: `access-control`, `devices`, `email-protection`,
   `data-protection`, `logging-and-detection`, `identity-lifecycle`, `engineering-systems`, `infrastructure`.

A product never decides the area on its own. An Azure DevOps test about who is a Project Collection Administrator
is `privileged-access`, not `engineering-systems`.

Inventory and health tests with no security theme of their own are `infrastructure`. When no area fits, choose
the closest and say so in the pull request, so the list can be reviewed.

## ResourceType

What a failing result points at. One key.

- `Tenant` when the test evaluates one tenant-, organization-, forest- or domain-wide setting. The result is
  about the environment.
- `Tenant` when the test checks that at least one policy of a kind exists, even when it lists the policies that
  satisfy it. A failing result has nothing to list.
- `Tenant` when the test evaluates the single default or global policy of a kind, because there is one of it and
  it applies to everyone.
- Otherwise the kind of object a failing result lists or counts: `User`, `Application`, `Device`,
  `ConditionalAccessPolicy`, `GroupPolicy` and so on. A test that evaluates every policy and lists the ones that
  fail uses the policy type.
- A test that counts objects for review (an inventory test) uses the type it counts. When no key names that kind
  of object and it is a one-off, use `Tenant`.
- A family test, which yields one result per instance, uses the type of the instance.

## Severity

The risk to the organization while the test fails. Not the effort to fix it and not the disruption of fixing it.

| Value | A failing result means |
| --- | --- |
| `Critical` | An attacker with no special position can take over the tenant, the domain or a privileged identity, or a secret is already exposed. Directly exploitable and wide in reach. |
| `High` | A primary control is missing or weakened for many users or for privileged identities, and common techniques such as phishing, password spray or consent phishing are enough to use it. |
| `Medium` | A defence-in-depth control is missing, or the exposure is limited to a few objects or one workload, or using it needs another weakness first. |
| `Low` | Hardening or hygiene with a small security effect on its own. |
| `Info` | The test reports a fact for review and makes no risk judgement. Info tests are left out of scores. |

Decide in this order:

1. **Reach.** Privileged identities or the whole tenant move the value up. A single workload or a few objects
   move it down.
2. **Directness.** Usable from the internet or by any signed-in user moves it up. Needing an earlier compromise
   moves it down. A password taken by phishing, spray or stuffing is not an earlier compromise: those are the
   common techniques `High` already assumes.
3. **Role of the control.** The main control for a threat rates higher than a second layer behind another control.

`Critical` is rare. If the description cannot say in one sentence how an attacker gets from the failing state to
admin rights or exposed secrets, the value is `High` or lower. A benchmark's own wording does not set the value:
a SHALL policy can be `Medium`.

Five cases come up often:

- **A test that passes whenever its data can be read** is `Info`, whatever the data is about. If the fact
  deserves a severity, the test should fail on it.
- **A failure that is only an outage or untidiness**, such as replication health, an expiring token or an unused
  object, is `Low`. It is `Medium` or higher only when the outage switches off a security control, and then it is
  rated as the loss of that control.
- **Alerts and notifications** are a second layer behind the control they watch, so they are `Medium` at most.
- **The same check in two suites** gets the same value in both. Usually the second is a shim that returns the
  first test's result and declares all of its values; see
  [Tests that another suite already has](./index.mdx#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).
- **The main control against an attack that starts from a stolen password** is `High`. A second layer behind
  that control is `Medium`. Number matching against MFA fatigue is `High`; showing the app name and location in
  the prompt is `Medium`.

Anchors from existing tests:

| Test | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Group Policy object contains a `cpassword` | `Critical` | Any domain user can read and decrypt the stored password. |
| No domain admin account has a service principal name | `Critical` | Any domain user can request a ticket and crack an admin password offline. |
| Legacy authentication is blocked | `High` | Password spray bypasses MFA for every user. |
| Number matching is required for Authenticator push notifications | `High` | MFA fatigue works against any user once a password is phished. |
| Authenticator shows the app name and location | `Medium` | A second layer behind number matching. |
| Users cannot register applications | `Medium` | Needs a signed-in user and a further step to cause harm. |
| MailTips are enabled for end users | `Low` | A small aid against mis-sent mail. |
| Disabled user count should be retrievable | `Info` | Inventory for review. |
| [EIDSCA.AP14 — users may read other users](/docs/tests/EIDSCA.AP14) | `Info` | Disabling `allowedToReadOtherUsers` is not itself a security finding. Review the restriction because it can disrupt collaboration, user lookup and default features. |

Microsoft's [Zero Trust Assessment](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment) rates many of the same
Microsoft Entra and Intune settings. Where it has a test for the same setting, compare your value with its risk
level and give the reason in the pull request if the two differ.

## UserImpact

How much the recommended fix disrupts end users. Administrators and the owners of applications are not end
users here. Developers are the end users of Azure DevOps and GitHub.

| Value | Applying the fix |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | End users notice nothing, or only administrators are affected. |
| `Medium` | Some users change how they work or meet a new prompt: a group loses a capability, users register a method once, a legacy client stops working for a subset. |
| `High` | Most users change a daily habit, or a mistake locks people out or stops mail or an app for many. Needs communication and a staged rollout. |

Omit `UserImpact` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## ImplementationCost

How much administrator work the recommended fix takes.

| Value | The fix is |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | One setting or one policy in one portal. Under an hour, with no dependency on another team, a licence purchase or a rollout. |
| `Medium` | Several steps: a policy that needs exclusions and a pilot, clean-up of a handful of objects, coordination with one other team. Hours to a few days. |
| `High` | A project: new licences, infrastructure or process, a migration of users or apps, or clean-up across many objects. Weeks or more. |

Clean-up that one administrator can finish alone in a sitting is `Low`. Clean-up that needs the owner of each
object is `Medium`. Turning on a plan that is billed by use is `Medium`: the click is easy, the budget approval is
not. Count the work of the fix, including exclusions and rollout, but not the time to decide.

Omit `ImplementationCost` when `Severity` is `Info`.

## Mitre

The MITRE ATT&CK techniques that the checked control prevents or detects. A list of technique IDs, or `None`.

- IDs only, in the form `T1110` or `T1110.003`. Tactic names are looked up from the pinned ATT&CK release
  (`powershell/assets/MaesterAttackTechniques.json`) and are never typed.
- Use a sub-technique when the control addresses only that sub-technique. When three or more sub-techniques of
  one technique apply, list the technique instead. Do not list a technique together with one of its own
  sub-techniques.
- List a technique only if the test's description explains, or plainly implies, how the control stops or reveals
  it. At most five.
- A test that implements a benchmark which publishes a mapping, such as CISA SCuBA, starts from that mapping and
  then applies these rules. An ID the pinned release has retired is replaced by its successor in that release,
  found by name.
- The description means the comment-based help and the Markdown file together.
- Use `None` for a test with no attacker behaviour behind it, such as replication health or an inventory count.
  An inventory test lists a technique only when the fact it reports is itself the precondition of that technique,
  such as accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication.
- A retired or unknown ID fails the unit tests.

## Control

Requirements of frameworks the test implements or supports, written `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`, for
example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.

- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
  tests check this.
- The first value that names a requirement in a framework file becomes the `Benchmark` of the result. Put the
  requirement the test is written for first, and any other requirement it supports after it.
- Use the same attribute for a test that exists for its own reasons and also supports a requirement: a Maester
  test that checks the setting a CISA policy asks for, or a CIS test that also supports a NIST control.
- When the key is a framework shipped with Maester (`cis-m365`, `cis-github`, `cisa-scuba`, `essential-eight`, `ism`), the requirement must
  exist in that framework's file. If it is new, add it to the file with its facts. The module build and the unit
  tests fail otherwise.
- Do not repeat the `Related` controls of a requirement. The framework file lists them and Maester adds them to
  the result.
- List a requirement only when a passing result is evidence for it. A test that checks one part of a requirement
  may list it; a test that is merely on the same topic may not.

A reference says the test supports the requirement. It never says the organization complies with it.

### NIST SP 800-53

A test may list the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls its setting implements, as `nist-800-53-r5:<control>`.

- Use an ID from the pinned list, [`powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json`](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/powershell/assets/MaesterNistControls.json):
  a base control (`AC-2`) or an enhancement (`IA-2(1)`). The unit tests reject anything else.
- List a control only when a passing result is direct evidence that it is implemented for what the test checks.
- Prefer the enhancement when the test checks exactly what it says: MFA for privileged accounts is `IA-2(1)`.
  Do not list a base control together with one of its own enhancements.
- At most three, best fit first. Never the policy-and-procedures controls (`AC-1`, `IA-1` and so on).
- A test that only reports a count, or checks health, licensing or tidiness, lists none, unless the count is
  itself what a control asks to be tracked: dormant accounts for `AC-2(3)`.
- A test that implements a CISA SCuBA policy does not list NIST controls. CISA publishes that mapping, the
  framework file carries it as `Related`, and the result gets it from there.

User accounts, except for break glass accounts, are protected by fixed or risk-based lockout mechanisms aligned to a maximum of five failed logon attempts, with either indefinite or automated lockout durations (ISM-1403, Guidelines for system access).

Online password guessing is cheap: an attacker who can try ten passwords per account before a lockout gets ten chances at every account in the tenant. Microsoft Entra smart lockout counts failed sign-ins per account, locks the account for the lockout duration when the threshold is reached, and counts familiar and unfamiliar locations separately so that a user at their usual desk is not locked out by an attacker elsewhere.

This test runs the same check as [CIS.M365.5.2.3.8](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.3.8) with ASD's maximum: the lockout threshold must be 5 or fewer (the `MaximumLockoutThreshold` parameter), where CIS allows 10. The Microsoft default of 10 fails. The ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud sets a threshold of 5 and a lockout duration of 60 seconds.

2. Set **Lockout threshold** to **5** and **Lockout duration in seconds** to at least **60**.
3. Select **Save**.

function Test-MtDisaIdleSessionTimeout {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that the Microsoft 365 idle session timeout signs users out after 15 minutes of inactivity or less.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The DISA Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop and Mobile STIG (V-273867) asks that the Intune service initiates a
    session lock after a 15-minute period of inactivity. Its check reads the idle session timeout of the Microsoft
    365 admin center (Org settings > Security & privacy > Idle session timeout) and requires 15 minutes or less.

    That setting is stored as the tenant's activity-based timeout policy. The check passes when the policy sets a
    web session idle timeout of no more than the given number of minutes (15 by default), and fails when there is no
    policy or the timeout is longer.

    CIS.M365.1.3.2 reads the same policy, but in hours, with a minimum of one hour, and it also requires a Conditional
    Access policy for unmanaged devices, which the STIG does not ask for. So this is a test of its own.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtDisaIdleSessionTimeout

    Returns true when the idle session timeout is 15 minutes or less.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/DISA.V-273867
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'DISA.V-273867',
        Title = 'Microsoft Intune service must initiate a session lock after a 15-minute period of inactivity.',
        Product = 'microsoft-365',
        RelatedProduct = 'entra',
        Feature = 'organization-settings',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1550.004',
        Control = 'disa-stig-intune-mdm:V-273867',
        Service = 'Graph',
        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
        Author = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Longest idle session timeout that is allowed, in minutes.
        [ValidateRange(1, 1440)]
        [int] $MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes = 15
    )

    $timeout = Get-MtActivityBasedTimeout
    $testResult = $null -ne $timeout.Timeout -and $timeout.Timeout -le [timespan]::FromMinutes($MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes)

    $value = if ($timeout.Timeout) { "$([math]::Round($timeout.Timeout.TotalMinutes)) minutes" } else { 'Not configured' }
    $link = 'https://admin.microsoft.com/#/Settings/SecurityPrivacy/:/Settings/L1/IdleSessionTimeout'
    $table = "| Setting | Value | Required | Result |`n| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
    $table += "| [Idle session timeout]($link) | $value | $MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes minutes or less | $(if ($testResult) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Users are signed out of Microsoft 365 web apps after $value of inactivity.`n`n$table"
    } elseif ($null -eq $timeout.Timeout) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "No idle session timeout is set. Set it to $MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes minutes or less in the Microsoft 365 admin center.`n`n$table"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The idle session timeout is $value. Set it to $MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes minutes or less.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

The Microsoft 365 idle session timeout signs users out of Microsoft 365 web apps after 15 minutes of inactivity or less (DISA Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop and Mobile STIG, V-273867, CAT II).

A browser session left open on an unattended computer can be used by anyone who sits down at it. The idle session timeout signs a user out of Outlook on the web, SharePoint, OneDrive and the other Microsoft 365 web apps, including the admin centers, after a period without activity. DISA asks for 15 minutes or less, which is shorter than the CIS benchmark's three hours.

The setting is stored as the tenant's activity-based timeout policy. Its check (`MaximumIdleTimeoutMinutes`, 15 by default) passes when that policy sets a timeout of no more than the allowed number of minutes. [CIS.M365.1.3.2](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.1.3.2) reads the same policy with a limit in hours and also requires a Conditional Access policy for unmanaged devices, which this STIG does not ask for.

#### Remediation action

1. In the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://admin.microsoft.com), go to **Settings** > **Org settings** > **Security & privacy** > **[Idle session timeout](https://admin.microsoft.com/#/Settings/SecurityPrivacy/:/Settings/L1/IdleSessionTimeout)**.
2. Turn on **Turn on to set the period of inactivity for users to be signed off of Microsoft 365 web apps**.
3. Choose **Custom** and set the period to **15 minutes**.
4. Select **Save**.

#### Related links

* [DISA Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop and Mobile STIG: V-273867](https://cyber.trackr.live/stig/Intune_MDM_Service_Desktop_&_Mobile/1/2/V-273867)
