function Test-MtDisaInactiveAccount {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that no enabled user account has been inactive for 35 days or more.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG (V-270204) asks that accounts are disabled automatically after 35 days of
    inactivity. Its check lists the enabled users whose last interactive sign-in (signInActivity.lastSignInDateTime)
    is older than 35 days, or who never signed in and were created more than 35 days ago, and is a finding when any
    such account is still enabled.

    This check does the same: it reads every enabled user, members and guests, and fails when one of them is
    inactive for the given number of days (35 by default). Microsoft Entra ID has no setting that disables
    accounts by itself, so the fix is a process (an access review of inactive users, or an automation) that
    disables them.

    ASD.ISM-1648 reads the same sign-in data for privileged users only, so this is a test of its own.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtDisaInactiveAccount

    Returns true when every enabled user signed in within the last 35 days.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/DISA.V-270204
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'DISA.V-270204',
        Title = 'Microsoft Entra ID must automatically disable accounts after a 35-day period of account inactivity.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'identity-governance',
        Area = 'identity-lifecycle',
        ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = 'disa-stig-entra-id:V-270204',
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
        Author = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Days without a sign-in after which an account must be disabled.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $InactiveDays = 35
    )

    $cutoff = [datetime]::UtcNow.AddDays(-$InactiveDays)
    $users = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -Filter 'accountEnabled eq true' -Select id, userPrincipalName, displayName, userType, accountEnabled, createdDateTime, signInActivity)
    $inactive = foreach ($user in $users) {
        if ($user.accountEnabled -ne $true) { continue }
        # The STIG's audit reads the interactive sign-in only.
        $lastSignIn = Get-MtUserLastSignIn -User $user -InteractiveOnly
        $isInactive = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn -lt $cutoff } else { $user.createdDateTime -and ([datetime]$user.createdDateTime).ToUniversalTime() -lt $cutoff }
        if ($isInactive) {
            [pscustomobject]@{
                userPrincipalName = $user.userPrincipalName
                UserType          = $user.userType
                LastSignIn        = if ($lastSignIn) { $lastSignIn.ToString('yyyy-MM-dd') } else { 'Never' }
            }
        }
    }
    $inactive = @($inactive)
    $testResult = $inactive.Count -eq 0

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Every enabled user signed in within the last $InactiveDays days ($($users.Count) users checked)."
    } else {
        $shown = @($inactive | Sort-Object LastSignIn, userPrincipalName | Select-Object -First 100)
        $table = "| User | Type | Last interactive sign-in |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
        foreach ($user in $shown) { $table += "| $(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $user.userPrincipalName) | $($user.UserType) | $($user.LastSignIn) |`n" }
        if ($inactive.Count -gt $shown.Count) { $table += "`nThe first $($shown.Count) of $($inactive.Count) accounts are shown.`n" }
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($inactive.Count) enabled account(s) have not signed in for $InactiveDays days or more. Disable them, or document why they must stay enabled.`n`n$table"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

No enabled user account in Microsoft Entra ID has gone 35 days or more without signing in (DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG, V-270204, CAT II).

Accounts that nobody uses are a gift to an attacker: a stolen or guessed password for a dormant account is unlikely to be noticed, because its owner never sees the sign-in prompts, alerts or mailbox changes. DISA asks that accounts are disabled after 35 days of inactivity.

The check reads every enabled user, members and guests, as the STIG's audit procedure does, and lists those whose last interactive sign-in is older than 35 days (`InactiveDays`), or who never signed in and were created more than 35 days ago. Microsoft Entra ID does not disable inactive accounts by itself, so the fix is a recurring process. [ASD.ISM-1648](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/ASD.ISM-1648) checks the same for privileged users with a 45-day limit.

function Test-MtDisaSignInBanner {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that the Microsoft Entra sign-in page shows the Standard Mandatory DoD Notice and Consent Banner.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG (V-270209) asks that the Standard Mandatory DoD Notice and Consent Banner is
    displayed before access is granted. Its check reads the "Sign-in page text" of the default company branding
    and is a finding when the banner text is not there.

    This check reads the sign-in page text of the default company branding (organizationalBranding,
    signInPageText) and passes when it contains one of the given texts. By default it looks for the opening
    sentence of the full banner and for the short banner that DoD allows where space is limited; the field holds
    1,024 characters at most. Comparison ignores case and runs of white space.

    The banner is a DoD requirement, so this test is meant for DoD tenants.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtDisaSignInBanner

    Returns true when the sign-in page text contains the DoD banner.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/DISA.V-270209
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'DISA.V-270209',
        Title = 'Microsoft Entra ID must display the Standard Mandatory DoD Notice and Consent Banner before granting access to the application.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'user-settings',
        Area = 'access-control',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Low',
        UserImpact = 'Low',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'None',
        Control = 'disa-stig-entra-id:V-270209',
        Service = 'Graph',
        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
        Author = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Texts of which the sign-in page text must contain one. Empty looks for the full and the short DoD banner.
        [string[]] $RequiredText
    )

    if (-not $RequiredText) {
        $RequiredText = @(
            'You are accessing a U.S. Government (USG) Information System (IS) that is provided for USG-authorized use only.'
            "I've read & consent to terms in IS user agreem't."
        )
    }

    $normalize = { param([string] $Text) ($Text -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim() }
    $organization = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'organization')[0]
    $branding = $null
    try {
        $branding = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "organization/$($organization.id)/branding"
    } catch {
        # A tenant without company branding answers 404.
        if ("$_" -notmatch 'NotFound|404') { throw }
    }
    $pageText = "$($branding.signInPageText)"
    $normalizedPage = & $normalize $pageText
    $found = @($RequiredText | Where-Object { $_ -and $normalizedPage.IndexOf((& $normalize $_), [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0 })
    $testResult = $found.Count -gt 0

    $link = 'https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/CompanyBrandingMenuBlade/~/CompanyBranding'
    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. The sign-in page text of the [company branding]($link) shows the DoD Notice and Consent Banner."
    } elseif (-not $branding) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The tenant has no [company branding]($link), so the sign-in page shows no banner. Customize the default branding and put the DoD banner in the sign-in page text."
    } elseif (-not $pageText) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The [company branding]($link) has no sign-in page text. Put the DoD Notice and Consent Banner there."
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "The sign-in page text of the [company branding]($link) does not contain the DoD Notice and Consent Banner. It reads:`n`n> $(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $normalizedPage)"
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

function Test-MtDisaPasswordLifetime {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Checks that passwords expire after 180 days or less on every verified, managed domain.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG (V-270239) asks for a maximum password lifetime of 180 days. The password
    expiration period is stored per domain (passwordValidityPeriodInDays); the STIG's note points to Get-MgDomain to
    read it.

    This check reads every verified domain that is managed (not federated) and fails when one of them never expires
    passwords or sets a period longer than the given number of days (180 by default). A domain that stores no
    period is reported for review: the STIG states that the Microsoft Entra default is 90 days, but tenants
    created more recently do not expire passwords by default, and the API does not say which applies.

    CIS.M365.1.3.1 reads the same setting and asks for the opposite, passwords that never expire, following
    NIST SP 800-63B. A tenant passes one of the two tests at most.

    .EXAMPLE
    Test-MtDisaPasswordLifetime

    Returns true when every verified, managed domain expires passwords after 180 days or less.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/DISA.V-270239
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'DISA.V-270239',
        Title = 'Microsoft Entra ID must enforce a 180-day maximum password lifetime restriction.',
        Product = 'microsoft-365',
        RelatedProduct = 'entra',
        Feature = 'organization-settings',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Domain',
        Severity = 'Low',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = 'disa-stig-entra-id:V-270239',
        Service = 'Graph',
        Lifecycle = 'Preview',
        Author = 'merill'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Longest password lifetime that is allowed, in days.
        [ValidateRange(1, 730)]
        [int] $MaximumPasswordAgeDays = 180
    )

    $domains = @(Get-MtDomainPasswordValidity)
    $applicable = @($domains | Where-Object IsApplicable)
    if ($applicable.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable
        return $null
    }
    $failing = @($applicable | Where-Object { $_.IsSet -and ($_.NeverExpires -or $_.ValidityDays -gt $MaximumPasswordAgeDays) })
    $unset = @($applicable | Where-Object { -not $_.IsSet })
    $testResult = $failing.Count -eq 0

    $table = "| Domain | Password lifetime | Result |`n| --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($domain in $domains) {
        $value = if (-not $domain.IsSet) { 'Not set' } elseif ($domain.NeverExpires) { 'Never expires' } else { "$($domain.ValidityDays) days" }
        $result = if (-not $domain.IsApplicable) { '⏭️ Skip' } elseif ($domain -in $failing) { '❌ Fail' } elseif ($domain -in $unset) { '❔ Review' } else { '✅ Pass' }
        $table += "| $($domain.Id) | $value | $result |`n"
    }

    if (-not $testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($failing.Count) verified, managed domain(s) let passwords live longer than $MaximumPasswordAgeDays days, or never expire them.`n`n$table"
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    } elseif ($unset.Count -gt 0) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "$($unset.Count) domain(s) store no password expiration period, so the API does not show which lifetime applies. Set the period explicitly to $MaximumPasswordAgeDays days or less.`n`n$table"
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -Investigate
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Passwords expire after $MaximumPasswordAgeDays days or less on every verified, managed domain.`n`n$table"
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    }
    return $testResult
}

input.content:
Passwords expire after 180 days or less on every verified, managed domain (DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG, V-270239, CAT II).

DISA requires a maximum password lifetime, so a password that leaked without anyone noticing stops working after a known time. In Microsoft 365 the password expiration policy is set per domain, and it applies to the verified domains that are managed by Microsoft Entra ID (federated domains follow the identity provider's policy).

The check fails when a verified, managed domain never expires passwords or sets a lifetime longer than 180 days (`MaximumPasswordAgeDays`). A domain that stores no period is reported for review, because the API does not say whether the default of 90 days the STIG mentions applies or, as in newer tenants, passwords never expire.

**This conflicts with CIS.** [CIS.M365.1.3.1](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.1.3.1) reads the same setting and asks that passwords never expire, as NIST SP 800-63B recommends. A tenant can pass only one of the two tests; run the one your organization is assessed against.

#### Remediation action

1. In the [Microsoft 365 admin center](https://admin.microsoft.com), go to **Settings** > **Org settings** > **Security & privacy** > **[Password expiration policy](https://admin.microsoft.com/#/Settings/SecurityPrivacy/:/Settings/L1/PasswordPolicy)**.
2. Clear **Set passwords to never expire (recommended)**.
3. Set **Days before passwords expire** to **180** or less, and select **Save**.

The admin center sets the period on every domain. To set one domain, use `Update-MgDomain -DomainId <domain> -PasswordValidityPeriodInDays 180`.

#### Related links

* [DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG: V-270239](https://cyber.trackr.live/stig/Entra_ID/1/2/V-270239)
* [Set the password expiration policy for your organization](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/set-password-expiration-policy)

Every Microsoft Entra role with an active or eligible assignment sends its Privileged Identity Management activation alert to the system administrators and the information system security officer (DISA Microsoft Entra ID STIG, V-270255, CAT II).

When an eligible user activates a role, Privileged Identity Management can email an alert. Sending it to the people who watch the system (DISA names the SA and the ISSO) means an unexpected activation, such as one made with stolen credentials, is seen while the elevation is still active. DISA asks for this on every role that has an assignment, not only the most privileged ones.

The check lists the roles that have an active or eligible assignment and reads the **Additional recipients** of each role's **Role activation alert**. A role fails when that list is empty. Set `RequiredRecipient` to the SA and ISSO addresses to require those exact recipients. [CISA.MS.AAD.7.8](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CISA.MS.AAD.7.8) and [CISA.MS.AAD.7.9](https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CISA.MS.AAD.7.9) read the same alert for the highly privileged roles only.

#### Remediation action

1. In the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com), go to **ID Governance** > **Privileged Identity Management** > **[Microsoft Entra roles](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_PIMCommon/ResourceMenuBlade/~/roles/resourceId//resourceType/tenant/provider/aadroles)** > **Settings**.
2. For each role this test lists, select the role and **Edit**.
3. On the **Notification** tab, under **Send notifications when eligible members activate this role**, add the SA and ISSO addresses as **Additional recipients** of the **Role activation alert**.
4. Select **Update**.

SKIP = {"Id", "Title", "Control", "Author", "Contributor"}

def target_attributes(target_id):
    files = [os.path.join(dp, f) for dp, _, fs in os.walk("tests") for f in fs if f == f"Test.{target_id}.ps1"]
    assert len(files) == 1, target_id
    src = open(files[0], encoding="utf-8-sig").read()
    block = re.search(r"\[MaesterTest\((.*?)\n\s*\)\]", src, re.S).group(1)
    lines = []
    for line in block.split("\n"):
        m = re.match(r"\s*(\w+)\s*=", line)
        if m and m.group(1) not in SKIP:
            lines.append("        " + line.strip().rstrip(","))
        elif not m and line.strip() and not re.match(r"\s*(\w+)\s*=", line):
            # continuation lines are not used in these attributes
            assert False, (target_id, line)
    return lines

for s in SHIMS:
    attrs = target_attributes(s["target"])
    name, base = STIG[s["fw"]]
    body = [f"        Id = 'DISA.{s['id']}'", "        Title = '" + s["title"].replace("'", "''") + "'"]
    # Keep the attribute order of the target: Product..Mitre, then Control, then the rest.
    before, after = [], []
    seen_mitre = False
    for a in attrs:
        (after if seen_mitre and not a.strip().startswith("Mitre") else before).append(a)
        if a.strip().startswith("Mitre"):
            seen_mitre = True
    body += before + [f"        Control = '{s['fw']}:{s['id']}'"] + after + ["        Author = 'merill'"]
    params = s["params"]
    param_block = "param()" if not params else "param(\n" + params + "\n    )"
    call = f"return {s['tfn']}" + (f" {s['call']}" if s["call"] else "")
    ps = f"""function {s['fn']} {{
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    {s['synopsis']}

    .DESCRIPTION
    {name} ({s['id']}, {s['cat']}): {s['title']}

    This test runs {s['target']} ({s['tfn']}). See the guide for what DISA asks and how the two compare.

    .EXAMPLE
    {s['fn']}

    Returns the result of {s['target']} with DISA's values.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/tests/DISA.{s['id']}
    #>
    [MaesterTest(
""" + ",\n".join(body) + f"""
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    {param_block}

    {call}
}}
"""
    md = f"""{s['summary']} ({name}, {s['id']}, {s['cat']}).

{s['why']}

{s['how']}

#### Remediation action

{s['remediation']}

#### Related links

* [{name}: {s['id']}]({base}{s['id']})
""" + "\n".join(s["links"]) + """

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
"""
    with open(f"tests/disa/Test.DISA.{s['id']}.ps1", "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(ps)
    with open(f"tests/disa/Test.DISA.{s['id']}.md", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(md)
    print("wrote", s["id"])

    raw = open(path, 'rb').read()

The build-website workflow builds and deploys maester.dev from main, so a merge needs no follow-up PR.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
  test may name the same requirements. An ASD test carries `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'` (or `ism:<id>` for a
  control outside the maturity model). Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its
  suite's framework. The engine builds `Benchmark` from the first `Control` that a framework file knows and adds
  that requirement's `Related` references to `Control`; do not repeat those, and do not add benchmark tags.
- A framework file is a catalogue, not a list of tests: `tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`
  (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json`,
  `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the generated `tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json` and
  `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json`, written by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1` from the ISM OSCAL release),
  declared in the suite's `suite.json` (`Frameworks`: `Key`,
  `Version`). It holds the framework's name and version and each requirement's `Id` and facts (CIS `Level` and
  `Profile`; CISA `Criticality`, `Upstream` and `Related` NIST references; Essential Eight `Level` and `Strategy`;
  ISM `Guideline`, `Section` and `Applicability`), never the text of a benchmark and
  never a `Tests` list. When a new test implements a requirement the file does not have, add the requirement in
  the same commit, or `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` and the unit tests fail.
```text
tests/                              The security checks: Test.<ID>.ps1 + Test.<ID>.md, plus suite.json, README.md and framework files
  <suite>/frameworks/<key>.json     The catalogue of a benchmark, one entry per requirement (asd/, cis/ and cisa/)
  maester/<service>/                MT.xxxx checks, one folder per service (plus drift/)
  maester/xspm/                     Exposure management; has its own suite.json (the nearest one applies)
  cis/                              CIS benchmark checks
  cisa/<service>/                   CISA SCuBA checks
  asd/<service>/                    ASD Essential Eight and ISM checks; frameworks generated by build/asd
  ad/<area>/                        Active Directory checks
  eidsca/  orca/                    Generated by build/eidsca and build/orca
  custom/                           Reserved for users' own tests; nothing is committed here

packs/<name>/                       Maester Packs that ship with Maester: maester-pack.json, suites, helpers, connectors

- `/maester` - Maester tests (`MT.xxxx`), with a subfolder per service such as `/entra`, `/exchange`, `/teams`
- `/maester/xspm` - Exposure management tests (MT IDs, with their own suite)
- `/cisa` - CISA tests, with a subfolder per service
- `/cis` - CIS tests
- `/asd` - ASD Essential Eight and ISM tests (`ASD.ISM-xxxx`), with a subfolder per service
- `/eidsca` - EIDSCA tests (generated, see below)
- `/orca` - ORCA tests (generated by `build/orca/Update-OrcaTests.ps1`)
- `/ad` - Active Directory tests
the rest keeps the benchmark's own punctuation, so a reader can search for the ID the benchmark uses.

| Test ID | Prefix | The benchmark's ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CIS.M365.5.2.2.2` | `CIS.M365.` | Recommendation `5.2.2.2` of the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark |
| `CISA.MS.AAD.3.1` | `CISA.` | SCuBA policy `MS.AAD.3.1v1`, without its version suffix |
| `ASD.ISM-1504` | `ASD.` | ISM control `ISM-1504`, written with a hyphen by ASD |

Use a prefix of your own. These prefixes belong to the tests that ship with Maester: `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `ASD.` and `MT1060.`. `MP.` is reserved for Maester Packs, third-party test packs
planned for a later release. A custom test with one of these prefixes still runs, with a
warning. A custom test that uses the exact ID of a built-in test is not run at all, and the built-in runs

The frameworks that ship with Maester, with the key to use in `Control`:

| Key | Framework | Framework file | Declared in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cis-m365` | CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark | [tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json) | [tests/cis/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/suite.json) |
| `cis-github` | CIS GitHub Benchmark | [tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json) | [tests/cis/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cis/suite.json) |
| `cisa-scuba` | CISA SCuBA Secure Configuration Baselines for Microsoft 365 | [tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json) | [tests/cisa/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/cisa/suite.json) |
| `essential-eight` | ASD Essential Eight maturity model (each requirement is an ISM control; `Level` ML1 to ML3, `Strategy`) | [tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json) | [tests/asd/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/suite.json) |
| `ism` | ASD Information security manual (ISM) (`Guideline`, `Section`, `Applicability`) | [tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json) | [tests/asd/suite.json](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/tests/asd/suite.json) |

Open a file to see the requirement IDs you can reference and the version Maester implements. NIST SP 800-53 has
no framework file; its control IDs are in
example `cis-m365:5.1.5.1`, `cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1` or `nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)`. Optional list. Any test can use
it: one shipped with Maester or one of your own.

- `Control` is the only way a test is mapped to a framework. A CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'` and
  a CISA test carries `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'` and an ASD test `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'`.
  Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its suite's framework. The unit
  tests check this.
| `Test.<ID>.ps1` | `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]` | One function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute. Reads the tenant, decides, calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail`, returns `$true`/`$false`. |
| `Test.<ID>.md` | Same folder, same base name | Description, `#### Remediation action`, optional `#### Related links`, then `<!--- Results --->` and `%TestResult%`. Shown in the report. |
| `suite.json` | Each suite folder (already exists) | The suite's ID, name, `Source` and help URL template. Do not edit for a single check. |
| `frameworks/<key>.json` | Beside the `suite.json` of the CIS, CISA and ASD suites | The catalogue of the benchmark: its name and version, and one entry per requirement with its level, profiles or criticality (ASD: maturity level and strategy, or ISM guideline, section and applicability). It does not list tests. A CIS, CISA or ASD check names its requirement in `Control`; add the requirement here in the same pull request if it is new, or the build fails. The ASD files are generated by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1`. |

Suite folders: `tests/maester/<service>/` (`MT.xxxx`; services such as `entra`, `exchange`, `teams`, `defender`,
`azure`, `intune`, and `xspm` for exposure management, which has its own `suite.json`), `tests/cisa/<service>/`
(`CISA.MS.*`), `tests/cis/` (`CIS.M365.*`), `tests/asd/<service>/` (`ASD.ISM-xxxx`, named after the ISM control the
check implements), `tests/ad/<area>/` (`AD-*`), and the generated `tests/eidsca/` and
`tests/orca/`. Every folder name is lowercase kebab-case; see the repository layout in
[the contributing guide](../../../website/docs/contributing.md#repository-layout).

# DISA STIGs

Checks that verify a Microsoft 365 tenant against the
[Security Technical Implementation Guides](https://public.cyber.mil/stigs/) (STIGs) that the US Defense Information
Systems Agency (DISA) publishes for Microsoft's cloud services:

| Framework key | STIG | Release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `disa-stig-entra-id` | Microsoft Entra ID STIG | V1R2 (30 Sep 2026) |
| `disa-stig-intune-mdm` | Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop and Mobile STIG | V1R2 (01 Jul 2026) |
| `disa-stig-intune-desktop` | Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop STIG | V1R1 (24 Sep 2024) |

DISA publishes no STIG for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams or Purview. The Defender for Endpoint and
Active Directory STIGs are not covered yet, and the device STIGs (Windows 11 and others) are checked on devices,
not in the tenant.

## Layout

- `suite.json` declares the suite (`DISA`) and its three frameworks.
- `frameworks/<key>.json` is the catalogue of each STIG: one entry per rule with its `Id` (the vulnerability ID,
  `V-270233`), `Category` (CAT I to CAT III), `RuleId` and `StigId`, and the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls of the
  CCIs the rule lists as `Related`. It holds every rule of the STIG, including those that no test checks.
- `Test.DISA.<V-ID>.ps1` and `.md` are the checks, in one folder, because the rules of one STIG are fixed in more
  than one product (the Intune STIGs ask for settings in Microsoft Entra ID and the Microsoft 365 admin center).

## IDs and mapping

A check is named after the STIG rule it implements: `DISA.V-270233` implements V-270233. Vulnerability IDs are
unique across STIGs, so the ID also tells you which STIG the rule comes from. The attribute names the rule in its
framework, `Control = 'disa-stig-entra-id:V-270233'`, and the framework file adds the rule's NIST controls to the
result. The `Benchmark` of a result carries the rule's `Category`, `RuleId` and `StigId`.

## Checks that another suite already has

Most DISA rules ask for a setting that a CIS, CISA or Maester test already checks. The DISA check is then a shim
that returns that test's result, with DISA's values as parameters where they differ (`DISA.V-270208` runs
CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 with a lockout threshold of 3 and a duration of 900 seconds). Rules the Intune and Entra ID STIGs
share (idle timeout, inactive accounts, lockout, MFA, password lifetime) are checked once and the other rules are
shims. See
[Tests that another suite already has](https://maester.dev/docs/next/writing-tests#tests-that-another-suite-already-has).

## Rules without a check

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| V-267315 (Intune Desktop: DoD banner the user must acknowledge) | The Entra sign-in page text shows a banner but cannot force an acknowledgement; DISA.V-270209 checks the banner. |
| V-267372, V-267373, V-267374, V-267375, V-267379 (Intune Desktop: notify the ISSO of account creation, change, disabling, removal and enabling) | DISA expects alerts from a log management server or SIEM, which the tenant does not show. |

## DoD-specific and conflicting rules

- The DoD Notice and Consent Banner (`DISA.V-270209`) fails outside DoD by design.
- The password lifetime rules (`DISA.V-270239`, 180 days; `DISA.V-267355`, 60 days) conflict with CIS.M365.1.3.1,
  which asks that passwords never expire. A tenant passes one side at most.

The checks with logic of their own are `Preview` until they have run against a DoD tenant.

## Summary

Add the DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) as frameworks in Maester, so a DoD or DoD-adjacent tenant can see its results by STIG rule in the report, the same way it sees CIS, CISA SCuBA and the ASD Essential Eight.

Most STIG rules for Microsoft's cloud services ask for settings that Maester already checks. So the suite is mostly **shims**: tests with their own ID and `Control` that return the result of an existing test, passing DISA's values where they differ. New logic is written only where no test checks what DISA asks.

## Which STIGs apply to Maester

| STIG | Release | Rules | In scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft Entra ID | V1R2, 30 Sep 2026 | 10 | ✅ Phase 1 |
| Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop & Mobile | V1R2, 01 Jul 2026 | 3 | ✅ Phase 1 |
| Microsoft Intune MDM Service Desktop | V1R1, 24 Sep 2024 | 12 | ✅ Phase 1 (still listed as current; mostly repeats Entra ID rules) |
| Active Directory Domain / Forest | V3R8 / V3R2 | many | Phase 2: maps onto the AD suite |
| Microsoft Defender for Endpoint | V1R2, 05 Jan 2026 | 25 portal rules | Phase 3, after checking which settings the APIs expose |
| Windows 11 and other device STIGs | | | ❌ Checked on devices, not in the tenant. The Intune STIG audit baseline that reports them is a separate idea |

DISA publishes no STIG for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams or Purview.

## Design (recommendations)

- **One framework key per STIG**: `disa-stig-entra-id`, `disa-stig-intune-mdm`, `disa-stig-intune-desktop` (later `disa-stig-ad-domain`, `disa-stig-ad-forest`, `disa-stig-mde`). Each STIG is released and versioned on its own.
- **Framework files** at `tests/disa/frameworks/<key>.json` hold every rule of the STIG, including those no test checks, so coverage is honest. Each rule records:
  - `Id`: the vulnerability ID, e.g. `V-270233`
  - `Category`: CAT I to CAT III
  - `RuleId` and `StigId`
  - `Related` NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls, taken from the CCIs DISA lists

  The files never hold the rule text.
- **Test IDs**:
  - Each test is named after its rule, e.g. `DISA.V-270233`. Vulnerability IDs are unique across STIGs.
  - `DISA.` becomes a reserved prefix.
  - The suite is one flat `tests/disa/` folder, like `tests/cis/`, because one STIG's rules are fixed in more than one product.
- **Opt-in suite (follow-up)**: some rules fail in every tenant outside DoD, such as the DoD banner and password expiry. The DISA suite should not run by default.
  - The engine has no opt-in suites today, so this first PR ships every test with logic of its own as `Lifecycle = 'Preview'`, which doesn't run by default.
  - The shims run like any other benchmark shim, since they only repeat results of tests that already run.
  - A suite-level opt-in (`suite.json`: `"DefaultSelected": false`, selected by `-Suite DISA`) is a follow-up that needs a decision on the engine design.
- **Conflict with CIS 1.3.1**: DISA asks for a password lifetime of 180 or 60 days; CIS asks that passwords never expire. Both tests stay, and each guide explains the conflict. A tenant passes one side at most.

## Coverage matrix (phase 1)

**Outcome counts:** 8 plain shims, 6 shims with a parameter, 5 new tests, 6 not automated.

### Entra ID STIG V1R2

| Rule | CAT | Requirement | Implemented by | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V-270200 | II | Session lock ≤ 15 min | DISA.V-273867 | Shim. The STIG reads the Azure portal's directory idle timeout, which has no documented API; the Microsoft 365 idle timeout applies to the portal unless the portal overrides it. The guide says so |
| V-270204 | II | Disable accounts inactive 35 days | **new** DISA.V-270204 | New test. ASD.ISM-1648 covers privileged users only |
| V-270208 | II | Lockout after 3 attempts, ≥ 900 s | CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 | Shim with parameter. **CIS 5.2.3.8 gains `MinimumLockoutDurationSeconds`** (default 0, so CIS is unchanged) |
| V-270209 | II | DoD banner in sign-in page text | **new** DISA.V-270209 | New test (DoD only) |
| V-270227 | II | Logs to Log Analytics / SIEM | CISA.MS.AAD.4.1 | Shim with parameter. **CISA 4.1 gains `RequiredLogCategory`**: DISA names 8 categories, CISA 12 |
| V-270233 | **I** | MFA for all users | CIS.M365.5.2.2.2 | Shim |
| V-270239 | II | Password lifetime ≤ 180 days | **new** DISA.V-270239 | New test (conflicts with CIS 1.3.1) |
| V-270255 | II | PIM activation alert to SA and ISSO, every assigned role | **new** DISA.V-270255 | New test. CISA 7.8/7.9 cover highly privileged roles only |
| V-270335 | II | No permanent active privileged assignments | CISA.MS.AAD.7.4 | Shim. CISA's highly privileged roles; the guide says to review the rest |
| V-270475 | II | Custom banned password list enforced and filled | CIS.M365.5.2.3.2 | Shim |

### Intune MDM Service Desktop & Mobile STIG V1R2

| Rule | CAT | Requirement | Implemented by | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V-273867 | II | M365 idle session timeout ≤ 15 min | **new** DISA.V-273867 | New test. CIS 1.3.2 works in hours and also needs a CA policy |
| V-273868 | II | Intune logs sent off | MT.1100 | Shim |
| V-285327 | **I** | Multi Admin Approval for device wipe | MT.1096 | Shim with parameter. **MT.1096 gains `RequiredPolicyType`**; the shim passes `deviceWipe`, `deviceAction` |

### Intune MDM Service Desktop STIG V1R1

| Rule | Requirement | Implemented by | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V-267303 | Idle timeout ≤ 15 min | DISA.V-273867 | Shim |
| V-267309 | Inactive accounts 35 days | DISA.V-270204 | Shim |
| V-267314 | Lockout 3 / 900 s | CIS.M365.5.2.3.8 | Shim with parameters |
| V-267315 | DoD banner, user must acknowledge | — | Not automated: sign-in text cannot force an acknowledgement |
| V-267334 | Intune logs offloaded weekly | MT.1100 | Shim |
| V-267341 | MFA | CIS.M365.5.2.2.2 | Shim |
| V-267355 | Password lifetime ≤ 60 days | DISA.V-270239 | Shim with parameter (60) |
| V-267372, 373, 374, 375, 379 | Notify ISSO of account create, modify, disable, remove, enable | — | Not automated: DISA expects SIEM alerting |

## Shared code

To avoid copying logic between suites, the Graph reads move into `powershell/internal/services/entra/`:

| Helper | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `Get-MtActivityBasedTimeout` | CIS 1.3.2, DISA.V-273867 |
| `Get-MtUserLastSignIn` | ASD.ISM-1648, DISA.V-270204 |
| `Get-MtDomainPasswordValidity` | CIS 1.3.1, DISA.V-270239 |
| `Get-MtRoleActivationNotificationRecipient` | CISA 7.8/7.9, DISA.V-270255 |

## Tasks

- [ ] Phase 1: Entra ID and Intune STIGs (framework files, suite, 5 new tests, 14 shims, 3 parameters, report and website registration). PR to follow.
- [ ] Run the Preview tests against a DoD / GCC High tenant and promote them to Stable
- [ ] Engine: opt-in suites (`DefaultSelected: false` in suite.json)
- [ ] Phase 2: AD Domain and AD Forest STIGs mapped onto the AD suite
- [ ] Phase 3: Defender for Endpoint STIG, after an API feasibility check
- [ ] Separate idea: checks that an Intune STIG audit baseline profile exists and reports results (Windows 11 STIG SCAP benchmark, Intune Advanced Analytics)

feat(disa): add DISA STIG frameworks for Entra ID and Intune with 19 checks

Add a DISA suite (tests/disa, IDs DISA.V-xxxxxx named after the STIG rule) with three
framework catalogues: disa-stig-entra-id (V1R2), disa-stig-intune-mdm (V1R2) and
disa-stig-intune-desktop (V1R1). Each lists every rule of its STIG with Category (CAT I-III),
RuleId, StigId and the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls of its CCIs as Related.

- New (Preview): DISA.V-273867 idle session timeout in minutes, DISA.V-270204 inactive
  accounts for all users, DISA.V-270209 DoD sign-in banner, DISA.V-270239 maximum password
  lifetime, DISA.V-270255 PIM activation alert recipients on every assigned role.
- Shims: 14 rules run CIS 5.2.2.2, 5.2.3.2, 5.2.3.8, CISA MS.AAD.4.1, 7.4, MT.1096, MT.1100 or
  one of the new checks, with DISA's values.
- Six Intune Desktop rules (acknowledged banner, ISSO account alerts) have no check.

Parameters for the shims: CIS 5.2.3.8 MinimumLockoutDurationSeconds (default 0, CIS unchanged),
CISA MS.AAD.4.1 RequiredLogCategory (default CISA's list), MT.1096 RequiredPolicyType (default any).

Shared Entra helpers in internal/services/entra: Get-MtActivityBasedTimeout (CIS 1.3.2),
Get-MtUserLastSignIn (ASD ISM-1648), Get-MtDomainPasswordValidity (CIS 1.3.1) and
Get-MtRoleActivationNotificationRecipient (CISA 7.8/7.9).

Register the suite and the DISA. prefix in the schema, pack tags, layout, lint, source and
framework unit tests, the report labels, the website generators, sidebar and home page, and the
docs. Regenerate the test builder data and the 2.x golden selection fixture.

Refs #2738
